body.statement:
The answer is negative.  Fix any \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}<\infty\), and suppose
\[
 0<\kappa<\frac{6373}{15369},
 \qquad
 0<\nu<\frac{39}{625},
\]
with a finite moment envelope \(C_{\mathrm{mom}}\) large enough to contain the bounded-moment counterexample in \(\texttt{thm:maximal-uniform-singular-mapping-failure}\).  Then
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \sup_{(P_j)_{j\geq1}\in\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})}
 \mathbb E_{P_n}\!\left[
  \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}
  \left|
   \Pr_{P_n}\!\left\{
    \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
         {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}
    \leq x\,\middle|\,\mathcal F_A
   \right\}-\Phi(x)
  \right|
 \right]
 =1.
\]
The failure is witnessed by stationary independent-over-time square proximal arrays having constant treatment effect, singular stacked limiting covariance,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)=\frac{39}{625},
 \qquad
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=V_s=1
 \quad(s\in\mathcal S).
\]
Consequently the singular Gaussian and scalar-HAC mapping handle cannot establish the proposed whole-array uniform selector-conditional normal approximation from the frozen assumptions; a uniform finite-row variance and distributional-stabilization condition is necessary for that conclusion.
body.proof_tex:
For a whole array \(P_\bullet=(P_j)_{j\geq1}\), define its row-\(n\) conditional Kolmogorov error by
\[
 \mathcal K_n(P_\bullet)
 :=
 \mathbb E_{P_n}\!\left[
  \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}
  \left|
   \Pr_{P_n}\!\left\{
    \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau}
         {\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}}
    \leq x\,\middle|\,\mathcal F_A
   \right\}-\Phi(x)
  \right|
 \right].
\]
Both terms inside the absolute value are distribution functions, so
\[
 0\leq\mathcal K_n(P_\bullet)\leq1.
\]

By \(\texttt{thm:maximal-uniform-singular-mapping-failure}\), for every sufficiently large integer \(q\) there is a whole array \(P_\bullet^{(q)}\in\mathcal M(0)\) such that
\[
 \mathcal K_q(P_\bullet^{(q)})\longrightarrow1.
\]
That theorem also supplies the stationary independent-over-time square proximal construction, constant treatment effect, singular limiting stacked covariance, and exact positive margins
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(D)=\frac{39}{625},
 \qquad
 V_s^{\mathrm{gap}}=V_s=1
 \quad(s\in\mathcal S).
\]

It remains to compare the bounded-gap classes.  By \(\texttt{def:panel-class}\), the only member condition depending on the numerical envelope \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\) is
\[
 \sup_{j\geq1}\sqrt j\,|L_{1,j}-L_{2,j}|\leq D_{\mathrm{gap}}.
\]
Every array in \(\mathcal M(0)\) has the left side equal to zero.  Since \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\geq0\), all its defining conditions also hold for \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M(0)\subseteq\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}}).
\]

Define
\[
 S_n(D_{\mathrm{gap}})
 :=\sup_{P_\bullet\in\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})}
   \mathcal K_n(P_\bullet).
\]
The universal upper bound and the preceding inclusion imply, for every sufficiently large \(q\),
\[
 1\geq S_q(D_{\mathrm{gap}})
 \geq\mathcal K_q(P_\bullet^{(q)}).
\]
The rightmost quantity converges to one.  Because \(q\) ranges over every sufficiently large integer,
\[
 1
 \leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}S_n(D_{\mathrm{gap}})
 \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}S_n(D_{\mathrm{gap}})
 \leq1.
\]
Therefore \(S_n(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\to1\), which is exactly the displayed conclusion.  The witness concerns this paper's own gap-split estimator over the broad reduced-form class; the common-subclass statement used in the preceding theorem does not assert the failure of any published fixed-role estimator or published guarantee.
